title: Civil conspiracy concerns concerted action by two or more persons that causes damage

content.overview: Civil conspiracy concerns concerted action by two or more persons that causes damage. The law distinguishes conspiracy to injure by unlawful means from conspiracy where the predominant purpose is to injure.
content.glance: Civil conspiracy concerns concerted action by two or more persons that causes damage. The law distinguishes conspiracy to injure by unlawful means from conspiracy where the predominant purpose is to injure.
content.study: Civil conspiracy concerns concerted action by two or more persons that causes damage. The law distinguishes conspiracy to injure by unlawful means from conspiracy where the predominant purpose is to injure.\n\nQuinn v Leathem is the leading authority. Crofter Hand Woven Harris Tweed illustrates careful analysis of purpose and means. Coordination alone is not conspiracy.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: Quinn v Leathem is the leading authority. Crofter Hand Woven Harris Tweed illustrates careful analysis of purpose and means. Coordination alone is not conspiracy.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: There is no single statutory tort of conspiracy. The claimant must establish combination, the required intention or unlawful means, causation and damage.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Two or more persons combine. 2. Common design. 3. Required purpose or unlawful means. 4. Causative damage.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Communications, contracts, meetings and transaction evidence may prove common design. Circumstantial evidence can establish combination.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Plead the precise conspiracy form and acts constituting the common design. Civil jurisdiction ordinarily applies. Limitation depends on the cause.

examples.title: Illustration 1 — Doctrine Satisfied
examples.body: Concerted action alone is insufficient; the claimant must prove the required purpose or unlawful means and causative damage.

examples.title: Illustration 2 — Boundary Defect
examples.body: Coordination is lawful unless the doctrinal requirements are established.

distinctions.title: Conspiracy vs Joint Tortfeasance
distinctions.right: Conspiracy concerns combination for a tortious purpose or means; joint tortfeasance concerns shared responsibility for the tort.

rows.left: Concerted action alone is insufficient; the claimant must prove the required purpose or unlawful means and causative damage.
rows.right: Conspiracy concerns combination for a tortious purpose or means; joint tortfeasance concerns shared responsibility for the tort.

rows.left: Apply the ingredients of the pleaded tort.
rows.right: Do not substitute the neighbouring cause of action.

misconceptions.trap: Any group commercial decision is conspiracy
misconceptions.correction: Coordination is lawful unless the doctrinal requirements are established.
